key.name: default-columns
key.description: Width, in character cells, that a terminal asks for when it is created. A new window sizes itself around this; already-open terminals keep whatever size their pane gives them.

key.name: default-rows
key.description: Height, in character cells, that a terminal asks for when it is created. See default-columns.

key.name: tab-position
key.description: Whether the tab bar sits above or below the terminal.

key.name: tab-bar-policy
key.summary: When to show the tab bar
key.description: always: keep the tab bar visible even for a single tab. multiple: reveal it only once a second tab exists. never: keep it hidden.

key.name: confirm-close
key.description: Ask for confirmation when closing a window that still has more than one tab open.

key.name: font-name
key.description: Pango font description used for terminal text. An empty string means the system monospace font.

key.name: theme
key.description: Name of the active terminal color theme.

key.name: scrollback-lines
key.description: Number of lines kept in the scrollback buffer. 0 disables scrollback.

key.name: scrollback-unlimited
key.description: Keep every line of output instead of the scrollback-lines limit. While true, scrollback-lines is left untouched so the previous limit comes back when this is turned off again.

key.name: scroll-on-output
key.description: Whether the view jumps to the bottom whenever new output arrives.

key.name: scroll-on-keystroke
key.description: Whether the view jumps to the bottom when a key is pressed.

key.name: cursor-shape
key.description: Terminal cursor shape: block, ibeam, or underline.

key.name: dim-inactive-panes
key.description: In a tab split into several panes, fade the text of the panes that do not hold the keyboard focus. The fade is drawn in the terminal's own background colour, so only the ink dims — empty regions stay identical to the focused pane. A single-pane tab is never dimmed.

key.name: audible-bell
key.description: Whether the terminal emits an audible bell.

key.name: shell-path
key.description: Absolute path of the program run in a new terminal. An empty string means the system default: $SHELL, falling back to the shell in the user's passwd entry.

key.name: login-shell
key.description: Start the shell as a login shell. This is signalled the traditional way, by prefixing argv[0] with a dash ("-bash"), not by passing a --login flag, so it works for shells that lack such a flag.

key.name: use-custom-command
key.description: Run custom-command instead of a shell. Shell integration is not injected for custom commands, since the command need not be a shell.

key.name: custom-command
key.description: Command line run instead of a shell when use-custom-command is true. Split into arguments with shell word-splitting and quoting rules; it is not interpreted by a shell.

key.name: launch-command
key.description: Text typed into a new terminal once it starts, followed by Return. It is fed to the shell as ordinary input rather than run via -c, so the session stays interactive and shell integration is unaffected.

key.name: cell-padding
key.description: Even interior padding, in pixels, between the pane edge and the terminal text on all four sides.

key.name: backspace-binding
key.description: Byte sequence the Backspace key sends. auto lets VTE pick from the tty settings (the previous, unconfigurable behaviour); ascii-backspace sends Control-H (0x08); ascii-delete sends DEL (0x7F); delete-sequence sends the escape sequence; tty sends the tty's own erase character.

key.name: delete-binding
key.description: Byte sequence the Delete key sends. Same choices as backspace-binding; auto reproduces the previous, unconfigurable behaviour.

key.name: cjk-ambiguous-width
key.description: Cell width VTE gives East-Asian "ambiguous width" characters: narrow (one cell, the previous behaviour and the Unicode default) or wide (two cells, matching legacy CJK fonts). Mapped to VTE's width 1 and 2.

key.name: preserve-directory
key.description: Whether a new tab or split starts in the current pane's working directory (reported by the shell over OSC 7). always inherits it unconditionally — the previous behaviour; safe inherits it only when the reported directory is on the local host, so a remote SSH directory does not send a new local pane somewhere that does not exist; never always starts at the daemon default ($HOME).

key.name: exit-action
key.description: What happens to a pane when its shell process exits: none leaves the pane in place showing the final output; restart runs a fresh shell in the same pane; close tears the pane down (the current behaviour).

key.name: new-tab
key.description: Accelerator that opens a new tab.

key.name: new-window
key.description: Accelerator that opens a new window.

key.name: overview
key.description: Accelerator that opens the session overview.

key.name: tab-move-left
key.description: Accelerator that moves the active tab one place to the left. Does nothing when it is already leftmost — the order does not wrap.

key.name: tab-move-right
key.description: Accelerator that moves the active tab one place to the right. Does nothing when it is already rightmost — the order does not wrap.

key.name: split-right
key.description: Accelerator that splits the active pane horizontally.

key.name: split-down
key.description: Accelerator that splits the active pane vertically.

key.name: close-pane
key.description: Accelerator that detaches the active pane, closing its widget while the session keeps running in the daemon.

key.name: kill-pane
key.description: Accelerator that kills the session in the active pane, after the same confirmation dialog as the context menu item.

key.name: zoom
key.description: Accelerator that zooms the active pane to fill the tab.

key.name: open-in-new-tab
key.description: Accelerator that moves the active pane out of its split and into a new tab of its own, without restarting the session. Does nothing when the tab has only one pane. The default is B for "break out" — tmux calls this same operation break-pane.

key.name: select-none
key.description: Accelerator that clears the active pane's selection.

key.name: read-only
key.description: Accelerator that toggles the active pane's read-only latch, stopping keystrokes from reaching its shell.

key.name: reset
key.description: Accelerator that resets the active pane's terminal state, recovering from a program that dumped raw bytes.

key.name: reset-and-clear
key.description: Accelerator that resets the active pane and clears its local scrollback view. The daemon's ring buffer keeps the history.

key.name: set-title
key.description: Accelerator that opens the Set Title dialog for the active tab — the same custom name the overview card menu's Set Title sets.

key.name: copy
key.description: Accelerator that copies the selection to the clipboard.

key.name: paste
key.description: Accelerator that pastes the clipboard into the terminal.

key.name: select-all
key.description: Accelerator that selects the whole scrollback.

key.name: preferences
key.description: Accelerator that opens the preferences window.

key.name: focus-left
key.description: Accelerator that moves focus to the pane on the left.

key.name: focus-right
key.description: Accelerator that moves focus to the pane on the right.

key.name: focus-up
key.description: Accelerator that moves focus to the pane above.

key.name: focus-down
key.description: Accelerator that moves focus to the pane below.
